items.q: Oral iron is listed as ferrous sulfate providing:
items.exp: Oral: ferrous sulfate: 60 mg elemental iron. (Book p810)

items.q: Oral iron on this page is:
opts: Given in non-dialysable patients and less effective
First line for all dialysis patients
items.exp: Oral: can be given in non-dialysable patients; less effective. (Book p810)

items.q: Match the following IV iron to its dose detail — 1) Ferric carboxymaltose  2) Iron sucrose  3) Iron isomaltose … A) 200 mg  B) 1 gm  C) 1 gm in 100 ml NS over 10-15 min
items.exp: IV: ferric carboxymaltose 1 gm in 100 ml NS over 10-15 min; iron sucrose 200 mg; iron isomaltose 1 gm. (Book p810)
1 gm in 100 ml NS over 10-15 min. (Book p810)

items.q: In the iron note, when serum ferritin is normal but anemia persists, the next step is to check:
items.exp: Note: s. ferritin — low → anemia; normal → anemia ± → TSAT = s. iron / TIBC × 100. (Book p810)
TSAT = s. iron / TIBC × 100; TSAT: transferrin saturation; TIBC: total iron binding capacity. (Book p810)
TIBC: total iron binding capacity. (Book p810)

items.q: A fall in serum iron means a fall in TSAT.
opts: False — TSAT rises when s. iron falls
items.exp: S. iron ↓ = TSAT ↓ — confirms anemia. (Book p810)

items.q: All but one are the IV iron preparations named on this page. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: IV: ferric carboxymaltose, iron sucrose, iron isomaltose. (Book p810)
